blocking_findings.finding: Two consecutive transport-class failures that become consecutive during startup recovery do not fsync an outage pause before the next reservation/dispatch.
blocking_findings.fault_injection: A transport_failure followed by a post-dispatch crash is recovered as ambiguous_transport. On the next run the adapter was dispatched once, no outage_paused event existed, and block 2/call 2 was reserved. Observed statuses were transport_failure, ambiguous_transport, completed.
blocking_findings.required_fix: After recovery and before any new reservation, reconstruct the consecutive transport count and, when it is at least two, fsync outage_paused with the frozen next cursor and raise OutagePause. Add a targeted regression test.

blocking_findings.finding: The required binding cannot satisfy live preflight in a clean committed tree because source_tree_digest includes the binding file while the binding must contain that digest.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Define and enforce a non-self-referential digest domain (for example, explicitly exclude only the binding artifact from both generation and verification), then regenerate and independently bind the resulting exact domain.

blocking_findings.finding: No executable live entrypoint constructs HermesAdapter and Orchestrator in live mode, accepts an explicit one-time outage resume, or supplies the specified commitment and ledger paths.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Provide a narrow tested CLI/command procedure for initial live execution and explicit resume. Do not authorize direct ad-hoc Python construction as the operational protocol.

provider_schema_assessment: Proportional subscription-OAuth schema is acceptable: operator attestation of no metered/extra-usage fallback plus durable local 90-call cap; it does not falsely require nonexistent provider-side booleans.
custody_limitation: The solver byte commitment and mode establish ordinary same-user masking only, not adversarial same-user separation or independent third-party custody.
